multiplechoiceresponse.p: A generative model produces a fluent paragraph containing a plausible but invented citation. This is best described as:

choice.div: Confabulation — fluent output that is not grounded in fact.
A perfect answer that needs no checking.
A sign the model is broken.

div.p: Generative systems optimise for plausible text, not truth. Every fact, number and citation must be verified before a learner sees it.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: Which should never be pasted into a public generative AI tool?

choice.div: Learner personal data and assessment records.

div.p: What you paste may leave the institution. Personal and assessment data stays in systems accountable for it — the LMS, not a chat window.

choiceresponse.p: Which are sound uses of generative AI in a classroom? Select all that apply.

choice.div: Drafting a set of practice questions for a facilitator to edit and verify.
Explaining one concept at three reading levels.
Deciding a learner's final grade without human review.
Letting a learner rehearse a role-play conversation.

div.p: AI is strong at drafting, reformatting and rehearsal. Decisions about a learner's progress stay with an accountable human.
